content: The PanoRef multi-origin optimizer implementation was reviewed and found to be algorithmically sound for normal graybox sets (8/10 architecture, 7.5/10 search correctness) but not production-ready for complex imported sets (4/10 readiness). Key strengths include deterministic area-proportional surface sampling, joint-pair mode that genuinely evaluates all legal coarse pairs ranked by bitset union, and a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, 24,576 fine samples). Six blockers were identified: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because candidate clearance uses object AABBs rather than actual geometry, causing any origin inside a large AABB to be rejected; (2) geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports (3M triangles ≈ 144 MB minimum packed, but actual JS objects/arrays are several times larger with GC pressure from per-triangle allocations); (3) geometry extraction still blocks the main thread before the worker starts; (4) the UI allows rewriting origins of already-captured panoramas, which is conceptually wrong since panoramas are rendered from their original origin; (5) reachableCoverage and combinedCoverage use different sample banks (coarse vs fine with seed+1), making the reachable upper bound mathematically inconsistent; (6) fixed-first mode does not enforce minimum origin separation. Additional refinements needed: the four-level refinement is not truly iterative (all offsets generated around original seed without updating center), local candidates can float between floors on sloped/multilevel terrain, and the optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules (optimizer evaluates angle/texel density but shader blends by distance). After review, the user instructed to rebase onto main, add allowed-floor-region mechanism, run a real complex imported-set benchmark with a 100K+ optimizer integration test, and spawn a subagent to disprove completeness. The assistant then updated the projected style materials shader to use coverage quality with explicit dominant-mode bias (replacing the stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF constant and projectedConfidence), removed the dead distance-only blend heuristic, and ran tests: multiOriginInteraction.test.ts passed (36 tests), full unit suite passed (42 test files, 371 tests), lint passed (tsc --noEmit), and build passed (vite build, 1777 modules). Notable test results include projectionCoverage.test.ts running both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture (39,235ms), and various WebGL pixel readback tests for occlusion cubemaps and projected-style materials.

The assistant implemented an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism to address the audit finding that imported-floor filtering still accepted large props (e.g., a 6×6 floor plus a disconnected 3×3 tabletop). Changes include: (1) adding `allowedFloorRegions?: CoverageBounds[]` to `CoverageSceneData` in `types.ts`; (2) adding `normalizeAllowedFloorRegions` and `triangleIntersectsAllowedFloorRegion` helpers in `surfaceSampler.ts`, plus an `isSelectedFloor` predicate that falls back to region intersection when no explicit flag is set; (3) adding `floorPointIsAllowed` in `candidateGenerator.ts` and gating candidate generation on it; (4) adding a toggle + X/Y/Z min/max inputs in `CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx` that pass `[floorRegion]` into `extractCoverageScene`; (5) adding a regression test `uses an explicit allowed floor region to reject a large prop top in one imported object` in `projectionCoverage.test.ts`; and (6) updating `README.md` and `docs/ui-revamp-regression-audit.md` to document connected-component filtering plus explicit allowed-floor bounds for ambiguous large tops. A first patch attempt failed because the README line it expected was already updated; the code patches then applied successfully. The base capsule records the broader context: the PanoRef coverage optimizer review found six blockers and required an allowed-floor-region mechanism, a real complex imported-set benchmark with a 100K+ optimizer integration test, and a subagent to disprove completeness; subsequent tests (multiOriginInteraction, full unit suite, lint, build, browser suite, and a 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer test) passed, and a goal-completion audit subagent later reported the two concrete holes (PR #23 conflicted remotely; imported-floor filtering still accepted large props), which the assistant acknowledged and said it was fixing with the explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism plus the auditor's large-top regression before publishing.

The assistant closed the coverage-optimizer audit hole by adding an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism (world-space X/Y/Z bounds) that gates candidate generation and extraction, plus a regression test for a large ambiguous top. After an initial patch attempt failed on an already-updated README line, the code patches applied: `CoverageSceneData` gained `allowedFloorRegions?: CoverageBounds[]`, `surfaceSampler.ts` added `normalizeAllowedFloorRegions`/`triangleIntersectsAllowedFloorRegion` and an `isSelectedFloor` fallback, `candidateGenerator.ts` added `floorPointIsAllowed`, and `CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx` added a toggle plus X/Y/Z min/max inputs. A first lint/build pass surfaced two TypeScript errors (a `key` prop on `Field` and `number[]` vs `Vec3` in the region mapping); the assistant fixed both with a `div`-based layout and `as Vec3` casts, then added a `floorRegionIsValid` check that shows an inline error and disables analysis for invalid bounds. Tests, lint, build, and the e2e coverage-optimizer flow were re-run and passed: `projectionCoverage.test.ts` (11 tests, including the 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer case), `multiOriginInteraction.test.ts` (36), and `uiFidelity.test.ts` (40) all passed (87 total), `tsc --noEmit` was clean, `vite build` succeeded, and the e2e test exercises the new floor-region toggle, invalid-bound error, and disabled analyze button. The assistant summarized that the floor gap is closed with a user-visible world-space floor constraint enforced during extraction and at every candidate projection, the 3×3 large-top regression passes, and invalid bounds are blocked at the UI.

Round-two audit found one concrete hole: allowed-floor controls remained editable during a running analysis, but edits did not cancel or invalidate the in-flight job, so a stale result could appear under newly displayed or invalid bounds. The assistant closed the race by disabling the floor-region toggle and all six X/Y/Z min/max fields for the full running state, and added a browser regression asserting the controls lock during the optimizer job and unlock afterward. Verification re-ran lint (clean), tests (uiFidelity 40 + projectionCoverage 11 = 51 passed, including the 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer case), build (succeeded), and the e2e coverage-optimizer flow (passed). Prior state carried forward: the coverage-optimizer audit hole was closed with an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism (world-space X/Y/Z bounds) gating candidate generation/extraction, a large ambiguous-top regression, and invalid-bound UI blocking; the rebased branch was force-pushed with lease and PR #23 is MERGEABLE. Remaining uncertainty: the round-two followup task wait timed out, so the audit round-two completion/acknowledgment is not confirmed in the captured events.

The focused 100K test gate, build, typecheck, and desktop/phone browser regression pass. Audit round four is initiated against the latest pushed commit and finds one remaining cancellation hole: stale extraction failures bypass the analysis-identity check and can overwrite a newer analysis state with `failed`. The assistant plans to add the same identity check to the extraction catch and a regression guard around that cancellation boundary, then publish and run another adversarial pass.
